serverInfo.instructions:
SEO Gets provides Google Search Console and GA4 data for SEO analysis, including branded vs. non-branded segmentation, topic clusters, and site annotations. 
		get_site_performance: Returns search and traffic performance data (clicks, impressions, CTR, position, sessions) for a site. Use it for questions about site, page, query, or topic performance over a date range. 
		list_content_changes: Returns annotations (notes) and recorded content changes, including Google algorithm updates, for a site. Use it for questions about what changed on a site and when, or to explain shifts in performance.
		Sites on the Super Sites plan store more than 16 months of history, so date ranges longer than 16 months are supported for those sites. For other sites, requests are limited to the data available for that site.

tools.description:
Use this tool for performance questions about a portfolio (a group of sites) or a site migration, instead of calling get_site_performance once per site.
Returns the same merged Google Search Console and Google Analytics 4 data as get_site_performance, combined across every site of the portfolio: rows with the same dimension values are summed, position is impression weighted, ctr and engagementRate are recalculated.
Add the 'site' dimension to get one row per site instead (useful to compare the old and new site of a migration).
contentGroup and topicCluster dimensions use the content groups and topic clusters saved on the portfolio.
Web metrics only include sites with a linked GA4 property. Unless explicitly asked, avoid querying the last 36 hours of data as it is often incomplete.
Only available for portfolios with up to 20 sites (see sites_count in list_portfolios); larger ones return a notice instead of data.

portfolio.description: Required name or id of the portfolio (see list_portfolios).

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 28 days ago.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 36 hours ago.

dimensions.description: Array of dimension strings to group by: site, date, query, page, country, device, contentGroup, topicCluster, sessionSourceMedium, eventName. 'site' splits rows per property instead of summing them. contentGroup and topicCluster use the portfolio's own groups. Optional.

metrics.description: Array of metrics to return: clicks, impressions, ctr, position, activeUsers, sessions, engagedSessions, engagementRate, keyEvents, revenue. Defaults to every metric the sites have data for.

filters.description: Optional dimension filters applied to every site. Omit this field entirely if no filters are needed.

branded_queries.description: Optional. true: only branded queries; false: only non-branded queries, using each site's branded keywords. Sites without branded keywords are skipped. Omit this field entirely if no filter is needed.

end_date.description: The inclusive end date used for the query in YYYY-MM-DD format.

data.description: TSV-formatted data. Columns: requested dimensions followed by the returned metrics. Rows sharing the same dimension values across sites are summed; position is impression weighted.

currency.description: Currency code the revenue metric is reported in.

note.description: Additional context, guidance, or validation feedback for the tool result.

tools.description:
Use this tool for every performance question, including GSC-only ones: request only search metrics (clicks, impressions, ctr, position) when web data isn't needed.Returns merged Google Search Console and Google Analytics 4 data for a site, one row per dimension combination.
Search metrics are clicks, impressions, ctr and position. Web metrics are activeUsers, sessions, engagedSessions, engagementRate, keyEvents and revenue.
Search and web metrics are joined on the requested dimensions, so a page or a date carries both its search performance and the traffic it produced.
Web metrics are only available when the site has a linked GA4 property, and GA4 has no query dimension: grouping or filtering by query returns search metrics only.
Super sites may have more than 16 months of data available. Otherwise, it's limited to 16 months of data.
Unless explicitly asked, avoid querying the last 36 hours of data as it is often incomplete, prefer 2 days ago or older.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 36 hours ago.

metrics.description: Array of metrics to return: clicks, impressions, ctr, position, activeUsers, sessions, engagedSessions, engagementRate, keyEvents, revenue. Defaults to every metric the site has data for.

filters.description: Optional dimension filters. Omit this field entirely if no filters are needed.

branded_queries.description: Optional. true: only branded queries; false: only non-branded queries. Omit this field entirely if no filter is needed.

tools.description: Lists a site's content changes in a date range as one timeline grouped by date: annotations (manual content changes the user logged, also called notes), automatically detected content changes (words added/removed, title/meta/heading/link changes), HTTP status changes, inbound internal link changes and Google updates. This is the only tool for listing annotations, content changes and Google updates: use it whenever the user asks about content changes, annotations or notes, what changed on the site, or Google (core/spam) updates. Pass event_types ['annotations'] to list only annotations; annotation items include the id needed by update_site_annotation and delete_site_annotation. Defaults to the last 28 days. To measure the traffic impact of a change, call get_site_performance for the affected pages before and after its date.

property.description: Required. The property domain or URL.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 28 days ago.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.

event_types.description: Optional list of types to include. Detected change types (filtered in the database): content_changed ('Content Changes': words and title/meta/heading/link edits), http_status_changed ('HTTP Status Changes'), internal_links ('Internal Links': inbound internal links added/removed), tracking_changes ('Tracking Changes': pages that started/stopped being tracked). Also annotations (manual content changes logged by the user) and google_updates. Defaults to all.

page_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring a page URL must contain.

content_group.description: Optional content group name. Only pages in this group (and annotations targeting it) are returned.

priority_only.description: If true, only pages in priority content groups are returned.

include_text_diff.description: If true, adds the added/removed text lines for up to 10 of the newest content_changed items. Slower; use only when key changes and word counts are not enough to explain what changed.
